fields.topology_type: Host-controller queue-pair architecture layered on PCI Express. Each NVMe controller is a PCI Function attached to the host's Root Complex via a PCIe link (or via a Switch Fabric). One controller = one Admin SQ/CQ pair + 0..65535 I/O SQ/CQ pairs.

supported_topologies.name: Single host + single NVMe controller, single port
supported_topologies.description: Figure 3 (Section 1.4): PCI Function 0 = NVMe Controller; one or more namespaces; the dominant consumer / client topology (M.2 SSD).

supported_topologies.name: Single host + multi-Function NVMe subsystem
supported_topologies.description: Figure 4: PCI Function 0 + Function 1, each presenting an NVMe Controller; shared namespaces between functions enable multi-path I/O and namespace sharing.

supported_topologies.name: Single host + multi-port multi-controller
supported_topologies.description: Figure 5: NVM subsystem with two PCIe ports each carrying its own controller; shared namespaces enable HA / dual-host / dual-port enterprise configurations.

supported_topologies.name: SR-IOV
supported_topologies.description: Figure 6: one Physical Function (PF) + N Virtual Functions (VFs), each presenting an NVMe controller; each VF gets a private namespace + access to a shared namespace; Virtualization Management Admin command (OPC=1Ch) configures VF resource assignment.

supported_topologies.name: NVMe over Fabrics
supported_topologies.description: Separate spec; same protocol shape rebound to RDMA (RoCE/iWARP/InfiniBand), TCP, or Fibre Channel transports; multi-host multi-target shared-storage topologies.

master_slave_role_summary.description: Initiates every command via SQ doorbell; allocates queue rings + data buffers; consumes CQEs.
Executes commands by fetching SQEs, accessing host memory, posting CQEs, asserting MSI-X interrupts. Also serves as PCIe Endpoint (or fabric initiator/target).

fields.interconnect_role: PCI Express Root Complex / Switch / Endpoint chain — addressing is by (Bus, Device, Function) for the controller's PCI Function. There is no NVMe-protocol-layer interconnect (no NVMe switch); fabric-level switching is done by Ethernet/IB/FC switches in the NVMe-oF case.

ordering_guarantees.within_a_command: PRP/SGL data buffer transfers complete before the CQE write (producer-consumer ordering on PCIe).
ordering_guarantees.across_commands: Commands within a single SQ are fetched in order but may be executed and completed out-of-order; controller communicates execution order indirectly via SQHD in CQEs.
ordering_guarantees.doorbell_ordering: Successive SQyTDBL writes must be monotonically non-decreasing modulo queue size; an out-of-order doorbell write is treated as an Invalid Doorbell Write Value event.

fields.memory_vs_peripheral_regions: Namespace logical block address space is the storage region. Each namespace exposes 1..2^64 logical blocks of configured LBA size (typ 512 B or 4096 B). No memory-mapped peripheral region is exposed to host except via the Controller Memory Buffer (CMB) and Persistent Memory Region (PMR) features when supported.

device_classification.boot_ssd: M.2 or U.2 with Boot Partitions support for UEFI-less platforms
device_classification.computational_storage: NVMe-attached compute / FPGA-on-storage devices (NVMe 2.x I/O Command Sets)
device_classification.scm_pmem_device: Storage-Class Memory device with NVMe PMR support
device_classification.nvme_of_target: NVMe-oF target subsystem behind a fabric (RDMA / TCP / FC)
device_classification.host_or_initiator: Host SoC PCIe Root Complex driving one or more NVMe controllers
